plan.contextChunk: This figure plots the probability simplex for a three-class problem on a set of three-dimensional coordinate axes. The axes are black arrows radiating from a shared origin: y_1 runs to the right, y_2 runs straight up, and y_3 runs down and to the left toward the viewer. Each axis carries a single tick labeled 1, and each unit point is annotated with a bold class name, Car at y_1 equal to 1, Bike at y_2 equal to 1, and Bird at y_3 equal to 1. A translucent pink triangle is filled in with its three corners resting exactly on those unit points, and the stretches of axis inside the triangle are drawn darker where the shading passes over them. The slanted face, not the volume it cuts off, is what carries the meaning: only points on that plane are admissible, the geometric form of requiring three nonnegative scores that sum to one. The drawing accompanies the definition of a classifier as a mapping from RGB images into the (K-1)-dimensional simplex, here with K equal to 3, where each vertex is an unambiguous prediction of one class and interior points are graded mixtures.

elements: y1 axis: black arrow from origin pointing screen-right, labeled y1 at its tip
y2 axis: black arrow from origin pointing straight up, labeled y2 at its tip
y3 axis: black arrow from origin pointing down-left toward the viewer, labeled y3 at its tip
shared origin point where the three axes meet
tick mark labeled 1 on each axis at unit distance from the origin
bold class label Car beside the unit point on the y1 axis
bold class label Bike beside the unit point on the y2 axis
bold class label Bird beside the unit point on the y3 axis
translucent pink filled triangle whose three corners rest exactly on the three unit points (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1)
dark red thickened axis segments from the origin to each unit point, where the pink shading overlaps the axes
draggable probability point (small sphere) constrained to the triangle surface
numeric readout of y1, y2, y3 beside the point with their sum fixed at 1

interactions.teaches: The admissible predictions form a flat slanted triangular plane cutting through 3D score space — the constraint y1+y2+y3=1 is a 2D surface, not a volume
Dragging the probability point across the triangle updates y1, y2, y3 while their sum stays 1 — class confidence is a constrained mixture: raising one class's probability forces the others down
Clicking a vertex label (Car, Bike, or Bird) snaps the point to that corner and drives the other two coordinates to zero — a simplex vertex is an unambiguous, fully confident one-class prediction

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Unit distance (origin to each '1' tick / class vertex) = 1.0 world unit; axis arrows extend to ~1.6 units so tips and labels clear the triangle. Simplex triangle vertices at exactly (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1); the point on it equals y1*(1,0,0) + y2*(0,1,0) + y3*(0,0,1) with y1+y2+y3=1, yi>=0 (barycentric coordinates). Orientation as in source: y1 axis along +X (screen-right), y2 along +Y (screen-up), y3 along +Z (toward viewer, appearing down-left); in the source the y3 axis extends visibly past the Bird vertex down toward the bottom-left corner. Colors: axes and labels black #000000; triangle fill salmon pink #f2a9a2 at ~0.55 opacity with no harsh edge; the three axis segments from origin to unit points drawn as thicker dark red #7a1f1f cylinders on top of the axes so they read as darkened where the shading crosses them; probability point a small sphere radius ~0.04, dark navy #1a2a6c for contrast against the pink; readout text black. Class labels Car/Bike/Bird bold black, placed just off each vertex: Car below-right of (1,0,0), Bike right of (0,1,0), Bird below-right of (0,0,1).
interactionPlan.notes: Implement the drag by raycasting the pointer onto the plane through the three triangle vertices, converting the hit to barycentric coordinates, clamping each to [0,1] and renormalizing so the point never leaves the triangle and the sum stays exactly 1. Render class labels and axis labels (y1, y2, y3, tick '1's) as camera-facing sprites; the click interaction raycasts against the Car/Bike/Bird label sprites and animates the point snapping to the chosen vertex. Update the y1/y2/y3 readout every frame during drag and snap. Draw the triangle as a double-sided transparent mesh (depthWrite off) so the dark red axis segments remain visible through it, and render those segments as separate cylinders rather than relying on blending.

discrepancies: The 'Car' label at the right vertex overlaps the italic y1 axis label, while in the source they are cleanly separated
The bold class labels (Car, Bike, Bird) partially cover the '1' tick annotations at each vertex, which are clearly visible in the source
An extra navy draggable probability point and a readout panel are added beyond the static source figure
evaluation.notes: Geometry, colors, and concept are faithful: the salmon simplex triangle, three axes, vertices, and dark-red origin spokes all match; the only weakness is label placement collisions around vertices, while interactions (drag constrained to the simplex, click-to-snap to vertices, live barycentric readout) are well-implemented and pedagogically apt.
action_items: Reposition the class label sprites and tick labels so Car no longer overlaps y1 and the '1' ticks remain visible beside each vertex
Consider making the extra navy draggable point toggleable or subtler so the figure can also reproduce the clean static source view

feedback.rationale: Scores are high (4.6 average, no failure modes), and the remaining issues are minor label-placement collisions and an optional toggle — polish that doesn't warrant another iteration.
